level.name: Beginner
level.description: Build the foundations needed to understand and use very common everyday English.

topics.title: Greetings and Introductions
topics.objective: Use common greetings, introduce yourself, and respond appropriately when meeting someone.
topics.theory: Greetings are expressions we use when we meet or leave people. Common greetings include Hello, Hi, Good morning, Good afternoon, and Good evening. When introducing yourself, you can say 'My name is Emma' or 'I'm Emma'. To ask another person's name, use 'What's your name?'. A common response when meeting someone for the first time is 'Nice to meet you.'

topics.title: The Verb 'To Be'
topics.objective: Use am, is, and are correctly in affirmative, negative, and question forms.
topics.theory: Use 'am' with I, 'is' with he, she, and it, and 'are' with you, we, and they. Negative forms include am not, isn't, and aren't. In questions, place the verb before the subject: 'Are you ready?' and 'Is she a student?'.

topics.title: Personal Information
topics.objective: Ask for and give basic personal information such as age, nationality, address, and contact details.

topics.title: Subject Pronouns and Possessive Adjectives
topics.objective: Use subject pronouns and possessive adjectives to avoid repetition and show ownership.
topics.theory: Subject pronouns are I, you, he, she, it, we, and they. Possessive adjectives are my, your, his, her, its, our, and their. Use them before nouns: 'my book', 'her car', 'their house'.
examples: Maria is my friend. She is kind.
This is John. His car is red.
We are students. Our teacher is Mr Lee.
They live here. Their house is large.
